NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice tracks cell voltage spread (V_max - V_min) at rest as the primary indicator of imbalance. My observable is the temperature-normalized voltage relaxation slope (ΔV/ΔT) during thermal transients, which captures the capacity fade and internal resistance divergence that voltage-at-rest alone cannot detect, as these manifest differently during thermal equilibration due to varying activation energies and charge transfer resistances in degraded cells.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is the Nernst equation and Arrhenius behavior: V(T) = V_ref + (α·ΔT) + β·ln(SOC), where α is the thermal coefficient (typically -0.3 to -0.5 mV/°C for NMC). A healthy cell should show consistent α across all cells. A 15°C gradient should produce a voltage spread of ~4.5-7.5 mV from thermal effects alone. A deviation >20% from this range indicates imbalance. (CALCULATED: based on typical NMC thermal coefficients and stated 15°C gradient)

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components:
- Existing temperature sensors (NTC thermistors) at each cell (USER CONSTRAINT: already installed)
- Existing voltage measurement system (USER CONSTRAINT: already installed)
- Existing BMS with data logging capability (USER CONSTRAINT: already installed)
- Standard engineering calculation module (no new hardware)

Procedure:
1. During module operation, record cell voltages and temperatures at 1 Hz sampling rate
2. When thermal gradient is present (>10°C across module), initiate measurement period
3. Calculate voltage relaxation slope (ΔV/ΔT) for each cell over 5-minute window after thermal perturbation
4. Compute standard deviation of slopes across all cells
5. Flag if any cell slope deviates >20% from module average slope

No new hardware required; only software implementation in existing BMS. (ASSUMPTION: BMS has sufficient processing capacity for real-time slope calculations)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensors and wiring
- Operability: SAME - integrates with existing BMS alerts; adds one new parameter to monitoring dashboard
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance points; same calibration requirements
- Cost class: SAME - only software development cost, no hardware changes

The approach maintains same deployment burden while providing earlier detection of imbalance development than voltage-at-rest monitoring alone.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Subject 3 identical test modules to accelerated aging protocol (1 cycle/day at 1C charge/discharge, 45°C ambient)
2. Apply controlled 15°C thermal gradient to each module during rest periods
3. Measure temperature-normalized voltage relaxation slope weekly
4. Continue until any module reaches 35 mV voltage spread at rest

Instruments:
- Data acquisition system (existing BMS)
- Thermal chamber with gradient control
- Calibrated reference multimeter

Pass/fail threshold: Module passes if temperature-normalized slope deviation remains <20% for entire test duration while maintaining voltage spread <35 mV.

Duration: 6 months (equivalent to 10-year calendar life at accelerated aging)

Kill criterion: Test fails immediately if any module develops 35 mV voltage spread while slope deviation <20%, indicating the leading indicator did not provide sufficient warning.
